symptom: An access rule WHERE comparing an attribute with a token other than [%CurrentUser%], or an association with '[%CurrentUser%]', passed check -p and exec and failed mx check (11.14.0, Production) with CE0161 "Error(s) in XPath constraint.": [Title = '[%CurrentDateTime%]'], [Title = '[%UserRole_User%]'], [D = '[%UserRole_User%]'], [Cnt = '[%DayLength%]'], [M.E_Kid = '[%CurrentUser%]'] where M.Kid is not a user.
file: mdl/executor/validate_access_rule_xpath.go (literalTypeProblem: xpathToken, tokenTypeProblem; literalTypeProblems: walkXPathMemberComparisons, currentUserAssociationProblem); test validate_access_rule_xpath_test.go
cause: literalTypeProblem returned early for every token but [%CurrentUser%], and literalTypeProblems only looked up attributes, so a qualified association compared with a literal was never judged.
insight: A quoted token is a string literal to mxbuild's type check: on a number it is refused like '5'. A date token is a DateTime and a [%UserRole_…%] token a user role; '[%CurrentUser%]' takes an association whose far end is System.User or a specialization of it (Administration.Account builds).
